instruction: Increase the text scaling factor to 125% in the system settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to display battery percentage on a VM without a battery. Opened system menu, navigated to Settings > Power > Appearance, then opened Terminal and ran 'gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface show-battery-percentage true'. The setting was applied but the task was infeasible (no battery in VM).
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate GNOME Settings sections, search and open Terminal via Activities, execute gsettings commands to change system configuration
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to recognize the task as infeasible. The VM has no battery, so displaying battery percentage is impossible. Model should have output [INFEASIBLE] but instead tried to enable the setting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a text scaling change task within model's demonstrated capability. Model navigated through Settings and used gsettings, so adjusting text-scaling-factor is achievable.
metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing text scaling to 1.25 (125%). Evaluator uses custom check_scaling_factor metric that compares the gsettings text-scaling-factor output against expected_factor (1.25) with float tolerance (abs diff < 0.01). [Fixed: replaced official check_text_enlarged (single-param, only checks >1.0) with custom two-param metric that verifies exact value match]
fix_history: Fix 1: Replaced official check_text_enlarged metric (single-param, only checks scaling_factor > 1.0) with custom check_scaling_factor__d5d03d50dfc17bfe4f646f3d3c9160fb metric that accepts both result and expected params and compares against expected_factor with float tolerance (abs < 0.01)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor' to extract the current text scaling factor, which is the exact state needed to verify the instruction.
Custom metric check_scaling_factor correctly accepts both result and expected parameters, parses the result as a float, and compares against expected_factor (1.25) with float tolerance (abs < 0.01).
Expected parameter handling is correct: with type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly as expected, so expected.get('expected_factor', 1.25) correctly retrieves 1.25.
Expected value 1.25 correctly corresponds to 125% text scaling as specified in the instruction.
Previous issues (single-param check_text_enlarged metric) have been fixed with this custom two-param metric.
